title: The Contact of Vienna Again
premise: Rosalind Sandoval, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives calls on a burner phone that shouldn't exist — each one in the voice of her mentor, Anselm Reiter, who died in Vienna nine years ago. The calls are a dead-man's-switch AI trained on Reiter's own recordings, built by the covert network he exposed: the Meridian Group, which grooms operatives through memory manipulation and then erases them. Following the calls across Vienna, Trieste, and a decommissioned Alpine clinic, Rosalind discovers she herself was Meridian's first successful subject, her four names the residue of four erased lives. In the climax she burns Meridian's archive from inside its Vienna vault, choosing to keep the memory of who she was rather than the safety of who she might have been, and hands the evidence to a journalist instead of the compromised courts.
about_author: Hazel Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed institutional files before walking away with nothing but her notes. She writes thrillers about people who keep records the powerful would rather burn, and she lives, deliberately unfindably, somewhere along the Adriatic coast.

chapters.title: The Number That Isn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind, living in Trieste as 'Clara Voss,' receives a call from a burner number with no service history. The voice is Anselm Reiter's — her mentor, dead nine years. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: cold dread wrapped in grief, the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Woman
chapters.summary: Rosalind audits her own security rituals and realizes the caller knows names she's never spoken aloud. A second call quotes her childhood — a childhood she believes she invented. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: the floor tilting under a life carefully built.

chapters.title: What Reiter Left in the Walls
chapters.summary: Flashback to Vienna, nine years earlier: Reiter showing Rosalind the first Meridian files before his 'accidental' death, and the promise she made to disappear rather than avenge. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: guilt recontextualized — her disappearance may have been engineered, not chosen.

chapters.title: The Voice Test
chapters.summary: Rosalind runs the recordings through voice-analysis software: the calls are Reiter's actual voice, not a clone — sampled from tapes she never knew existed. Someone built a machine from a dead man's confessions. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Contact of Vienna
chapters.summary: Rosalind returns to Vienna under a fifth name and meets her old fixer, Marek, who warns that Meridian's successors now run half the city's private-security industry. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: homecoming as infiltration, nostalgia curdling into vigilance.

chapters.title: The Clinic Above the Snowline
chapters.summary: Following coordinates from the calls, Rosalind finds a decommissioned Alpine clinic where Meridian ran 'memory consolidation' — and a surviving patient who recognizes her face but calls her a name she's never used. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: the first crack in her origin story.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Patient's Ledger
chapters.summary: The patient, Ilse, keeps a handwritten ledger of everything the clinic erased. Her entries describe 'Subject R' — a woman who arrived with four names and left with one. POV Ilse. Emotional beat: quiet, devastating witness; Rosalind's history reflected in a stranger's handwriting.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind confronts the ledger: before Rosalind Sandoval, she was someone else entirely, and Meridian didn't erase that life — she volunteered it away. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: rage at Reiter for complicity, grief for the woman she agreed to stop being.

chapters.title: Marek's Price
chapters.summary: Marek agrees to get Rosalind into a Meridian front company's server room — but demands she recover his own erased file first, revealing he's a former subject too. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two damaged people bargaining in the dark.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers to Reiter's Voice
chapters.summary: A live call comes in while Rosalind is surveilling the front company — and a Meridian operative answers the same line, proving the network uses the dead-man's-switch AI as internal command. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: the trap reveals its shape; the phone is both lure and leash.

chapters.title: Burner Protocol
chapters.summary: Rosalind reverse-engineers the switch: Reiter seeded it to activate only if Meridian resumed operations, and it's been calling every erased subject it can still find. She's not the target — she's the messenger. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: from hunted to chosen, terror becoming responsibility.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Can't Be Bought
chapters.summary: Rosalind approaches Nadia Ferro, an investigative journalist whose last Meridian story died in court. Nadia agrees to publish — but only with primary evidence Rosalind doesn't yet have. POV Nadia. Emotional beat: outside perspective on Rosalind's damage; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Vault Under the Danube
chapters.summary: Marek's intel places Meridian's original archive in a flood-controlled vault beneath a Vienna power station, accessible for ninety minutes during a scheduled maintenance window. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: the plan crystallizes; the countdown begins.

chapters.title: Ilse Disappears
chapters.summary: Meridian's cleaners reach Ilse's apartment hours before Rosalind can move her. The ledger survives; Ilse doesn't. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief weaponized — the cost of hesitation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Anselm Reiter's Hands
chapters.summary: Rosalind tracks the operative who answered Reiter's line: Dr. Lukas Brandt, the clinic's surviving architect, who reveals Reiter is alive — held as Meridian's insurance policy, his memory wiped so thoroughly he no longer knows his own name. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: the dead mentor resurrected as a hostage; hope and cruelty in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: The vault operation goes in: Marek cuts power, Rosalind descends into the archive, and finds Reiter's original confession tapes alongside forty years of erased lives — including her own intake file, signed in her handwriting. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: claustrophobic triumph turning to vertigo as she reads her own consent.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Vault
chapters.summary: Brandt offers Rosalind a trade: Reiter's location for the archive. She can restore her erased memories in the clinic's last working chair — or destroy the archive and lose herself forever. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: the novel's moral fulcrum; justice versus self-knowledge.

chapters.title: What She Chose to Keep
chapters.summary: Rosalind copies the archive to Nadia, then torches the vault's originals — and takes the memory treatment, not to erase but to recover, gambling her mind on Meridian's own machine. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: burning the bridge behind her; faith in the self she's about to meet.

chapters.title: The Man by the River
chapters.summary: Recovered, Rosalind finds Reiter — an old man feeding gulls on the Danube who doesn't know her, but whose hands still tap the old signal code. She gives him back his name; he gives her the last passphrase. POV Reiter. Emotional beat: forgiveness without recognition; the debt repaid in both directions.

chapters.title: Meridian Answers
chapters.summary: Meridian's directors move to kill the story and everyone attached: Marek is taken, Nadia's office raided, and the dead-man's-switch begins broadcasting the archive to every subject simultaneously — Rosalind's contingency, triggered early. POV alternating Rosalind/Nadia. Emotional beat: the net closing and the counterattack igniting at once.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: In the climax, Rosalind walks into Meridian's Vienna headquarters carrying the switch as a live microphone, lets the directors incriminate themselves on their own command channel, and walks out as forty erased subjects converge on the city, each holding the same evidence. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: cold, controlled fury; justice executed in broad daylight.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Months later: trials begin abroad, Marek is freed, Nadia's byline runs the archive in full, and Rosalind — keeping Reiter's surname as her own — takes a burner phone that rings with work no one wants attributed. She answers. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: resolution as continuation; a woman finally at home in a name she chose herself.
